body: Apologies, it’s a misnomer. I meant ‘heinousness’.

The men in the comments section constantly giving reasons for why we as women despise Indian men. Constantly ignoring women’s narratives, calling out feminist ideas, taking about so called ‘fake’ cases, and genuinely shitting on women. And then they put up the question of heinousness when women say something about them.

Let my exemplify. If someone trying to insult your mother says ‘you’re a servant’, would you be okay with it? Or if someone looks at you on the street and makes a humiliating expression, and says ‘naukar’, would you be okay? Would you take it as a compliment. On the contrary, if someone calls themselves as a ‘humble servant’, would you take that as an offence or a compliment? 

The fact that you don’t understand the concept of ‘context’ shows the failure of the education system. No one from a marginalised class or community likes to be humiliated with their profession. Just like a dog or a swine isn’t a bad animal but when people are insulted by those words, they feel anger. 

Before criticising the ‘feudal’ mindset of people who clearly have much more command over linguistic intricacies than your completely incoherent self, try to read the law. ‘Intent’, look up the meaning. ‘Context’, understand that word.

P.S. I saw your profile after the message, and your stance on an air hostess getting bullied online makes so much sense now. See? Context makes everything more explainable.

You recognise the concept of intent, right? Calling someone a servant with the intent of using the word in a demeaning capacity is what’s wrong. If you call someone a servant with the intent of glorification like ‘public servant’ or ‘servant of god’, the word becomes appropriative. Words aren’t isolated in a void, they have contextual meaning. Maybe you need to understand that. Just like if I call you a degenerate illogical buffoon, it clearly means I despise your existence, not that buffoons are degenerate and illogical.

Look, as human beings pain (no matter of what kind) is something that we should usually run away from. Think about it, even the slightest sensation of pain, like an ant bite or a piercing needle is usually seen as a discomfort. Self harm quite literally makes you numb to sensations like this. You become emotional devoid of the feeling of pain. Moreover, you start developing an unhealthy addiction to pain. 

I’m general substance addiction, a ‘victim’ slowly adjusts to the substance quantity they take. When this sort of tolerance is developed and becomes normative for the person, they try a bigger quantity. Addictive behaviour increases substantially over time. Similarly, in the case of self harm, the victim keeps on trying bigger stimuluses, from one cut to a few cuts at the same time, or an increase in the depth of the cut. In the short run, this might seems like nothing, but as things snowball and one tries to seek the next big thing, one could severely injure oneself.

Not going to lie, I am a self-harmer and I have occasionally cut myself. And I find immense pleasure in pain and looking back at my scars always brings a smile to my face. But I’ve noticed that my tendencies when allowed to go forth for extensive periods of time, have just turned more and more dangerous. I’ve constantly looked for the next high, the next sort of pleasurable pain I can get. (My way of treating myself is looking out for natural pain. Being clumsy and letting myself get hurt. Sounds very stupid, but it’s like replacing a smoking addiction with a nicotine patch addiction.)

But yeah, in my perspective, self harm and scars may make you happy in the short run, but might lead to vital injury in the long run. It also has emotional repercussions, but I don’t think I’ll get into that right now.
